scope: GD-0042 M01 source and existing-test inventory of SQL callers. This is not a release attestation, a cross-package runtime test, or a claim that the proposed native v1 or PostgreSQL 18 reference surface is implemented.
non_claims: SQL remains an independently supported input interface; native engine operations do not generate SQL text.
The bounded embedded SQL grammar is not general PostgreSQL 18 compatibility. The server wire protocol and its pinned driver tests establish only the documented preview subset.
Existing test references are evidence locations. These inventory tests do not rerun those packages or qualify production networks, storage hardware, arbitrary drivers, or deployment security.

interfaces.authority: Trusted local Admin capability. Generic relational SQL grants no finite task authority and never exposes the reserved repair tables.
implemented: Typed positional parameters, CREATE TABLE with primary key, single-row INSERT, full-primary-key UPDATE/DELETE, bounded SELECT, explicit transactions and expected-version writes.
Bounded aliases, indexed inner/left joins, global COUNT/SUM/MIN/MAX, qualified scalar sorting and EXPLAIN use the relational query engine.
Prepared handles are fenced by database domain, catalog epoch and transaction identity; failed explicit transactions require rollback.
restrictions: Only bool, signed int2/int4/int8, text, bytea and NULL; no coercive type fallback, timestamps, decimal, JSON or UUID.
No unbounded reads or writes, generic DDL evolution, multi-row INSERT, expression assignments, PK changes, comments, multi-statements, upsert or RETURNING.
Successful SQL equal-value UPDATE still advances the row version. Native no-op preservation does not redefine this SQL contract.
Distinct-table joins report the reserved giggles_join authorization target; gateways must not authorize only the first source.
unverified: General PostgreSQL compatibility and proposed native v1 language coverage are outside this implemented profile.

interfaces.endpoint: local::admin AdminCommand::{Sql,SqlBatch,Catalog}; local::sql_session; trusted giggles admin PATH JSON/@file CLI
interfaces.authority: Trusted local Admin handle or database-file access; JSON is an adapter, not remote authentication.
implemented: Versioned replies, typed params and optional expected_version. SqlBatch executes ordered statements in one session; explicit BEGIN/COMMIT supplies transaction boundaries.
restrictions: One-shot Sql cannot leave an open transaction. Batch permits at most 256 statements and rejects an open transaction at completion.
Batch has no implicit atomicity: earlier autocommits survive a later error; explicit uncommitted staging is rolled back when the session drops.
The underlying relational subset and reserved names remain enforced.

interfaces.authority: Only an in-process Admin handle can create a session. Handle IDs are registry references, not remote credentials. The caller owns valid C pointers and returned buffer lifetimes.

implemented: Persistent REPL transactions; bounded semicolon-terminated scripts; typed parameter file and CAS for single --sql.

core_sql_cases.sql: SELECT title, active FROM app WHERE id=$1
core_sql_cases.reason: A full primary-key equality may omit LIMIT; parameters retain their scalar types.

core_sql_cases.sql: SELECT id FROM app ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 2

core_sql_cases.reason: A full scan without LIMIT streams every row in primary-key order (GD-0058 B2, 1ca74e2).
A searched DELETE without a primary-key point is accepted and statement-atomic (GD-0058 B5); this one matches no rows.

core_sql_cases.sql: CREATE TABLE deliveries (id BIGINT PRIMARY KEY)
core_sql_cases.reason: Finite repair tables do not become generic application relations.
The lexer skips -- line comments and nested /* */ block comments (GD-0059 E1 A4, 2ae5e74), so this full scan returns every row.

core_sql_cases.sql: SELECT * FROM app; DELETE FROM app WHERE id=1
core_sql_cases.reason: One SQL statement per core call.

core_sql_cases.sql: CREATE TABLE dated (id TIMESTAMPTZ PRIMARY KEY)
core_sql_cases.reason: The proposed reference scalar family exceeds the current SQL type profile.
